eyebrow: Every test in this chapter follows this
A permutation test: the observed gap
code:
old = rng.normal(52, 15, 40).round(2)
new = rng.normal(58, 15, 40).round(2)
obs = new.mean() - old.mean()
print(round(obs, 2))   # 5.62
caption: If the email truly does nothing, the labels "old"/"new" are meaningless -- shuffle them.

code:
pooled = np.concatenate([old, new])
for i in range(10000):
    rng.shuffle(pooled)
    diffs[i] = pooled[40:].mean() - pooled[:40].mean()
p = (np.abs(diffs) >= abs(obs)).mean()
print(p)   # 0.0343
caption: Only ~3.4% of random shuffles produced a gap this large -- the p-value (next lesson).

eyebrow: What a test does and doesn't tell you

steps.label: SMALL p -> HARD TO EXPLAIN BY CHANCE
steps.sub: Not the size of the effect, not causation
